raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Part **2/n** of the Kimi K3 / Dist-MoE training stack. Targets `main` after #5674 merged; the review diff contains only this feature.

human notes: 

add an knob to expose backward-prefetch policy when ep is enabled. previously, backward-prefetch is always on when ep is on, after this pr, one can disable it to reduce peak memory. 

## Why

Expert-parallel decoder setup always wires explicit backward prefetch. Memory-constrained pipeline/CUDA-graph recipes cannot opt out of gathering the next parameter unit early. Leaving explicit targets empty does not disable prefetch: FSDP uses its implicit fallback.

Example:

```python
ParallelismConfig(
    expert_parallel_degree=4,
    fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False,
)
# Current parameters are still gathered when backward needs them.
# Do not gather the next backward parameter unit early.
# Forward-prefetch and reshard/reduction policies are unchanged.
```

## What changed

- Add default-on `fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch` and propagate `enable_backward_prefetch` through common decoder and MTP FSDP setup.
- Build neighboring source/target pairs when enabled, or self-pairs for every FSDP module when disabled. One shared loop applies the targets with the public FSDP setter.
- A self-pair `(A, A)` becomes `A.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch([A])`. The nonempty target list suppresses implicit prefetch; A's parameters are already prepared by its own pre-backward hook, so the self-prefetch adds no all-gather.
- Extend the existing wiring test to empty, one-layer, and multi-layer stages while retaining its forward-prefetch and decoder/MTP policy checks.

## Alternatives considered

- An empty target list retains FSDP's implicit fallback rather than disabling prefetch.
- Disabling forward prefetch would change a separate overlap policy.
- Calling private FSDP state APIs is unnecessary: self-targets use the existing public setter.

## User-facing changes

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Default `fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=True` with EP | Preserve the existing backward-prefetch target order. |
| `fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False` with EP | Suppress explicit and implicit backward prefetch, trading overlap for lower peak unsharded-parameter memory. |
| Without EP | This option has no effect. |

The shorter knob name reflects its scope: disabling it suppresses both explicit and implicit backward prefetch, not only explicit targets.

## Numerics

No model arithmetic, parameter layout, reduction dtype, forward-prefetch policy, or reshard policy changes.

Real two-rank GB300 checks compared the refactored setup against the preceding 2/n implementation at `3449bed04583bc21f37307b978ed2d268e20d191`, with both prefetch settings. Three updates with two accumulation microbatches, seed 42, strict deterministic algorithms, FP32 resident state/reduction, and BF16 compute views produced exact loss, gradient-norm, local gradient-shard, and updated parameter-shard equality.

| Workload | GPUs | Before/after result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3 EP2/FSDP2, no activation checkpointing, both policies | 2 | Bitwise identical. |
| FullAC Llama3 dense stage under an EP2/FSDP2 mesh, both policies | 2 | Bitwise identical. |

These are small numerical checks, not full-scale memory/performance or fresh CUDA-graph replay acceptance. No isolated end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Testing

**79 CPU checks passed** for the current local amendment on `main` (`ff96670a2`):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/config/test_parallelism_config.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_fsdp.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_parallelism_context.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/deepseek_v4/test_deepseek_v4_mtp.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/observability/test_sdc_replayer.py
```

An additional local comparison passed **192 exact ordered target-plan cases** against the preceding implementation: 0/1/3 layers, optional embedding/norm/head, tied/untied weights, EP1/EP2, both policies, and nested FSDP units.

All non-type pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Type checking of the local amendment found no new FSDP errors.

## Known issues / landing gates

The same three local Pyrefly errors were independently reproduced on unchanged upstream: missing `torch_checkpointing.checkpoint_writer.CallbackArgs`, its related callback signature mismatch, and optional `video.stream.time_base` multiplication. No unrelated source or dependency workaround is included.

Fresh CUDA-graph replay and large-scale memory/performance are not separately verified at this prefix. A maintainer still needs to review the core changes.

## Stack

[#5674](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5674) has merged. This PR now targets `main`. Next: [#5676](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5676).

nodes.body:
**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 3m 9s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41135764218)

---
**Request changes** -- see the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5675#pullrequestreview) for details.

**Verdict: Request changes** -- No recipe in the repo or the stack turns the new knob off, and it silently does nothing without EP. The mechanism works, but it relies on undocumented FSDP2 behavior and has no upstream TODO.

**What this PR does.** It adds `ParallelismConfig.fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch` (default `True`) and passes it to `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` and the MTP wrapper. With EP on and the flag `True`, the existing backward-prefetch chain (lm_head -> last layer -> ... -> first layer -> tok_embeddings) is rebuilt as a list of pairs. I checked the order against `main` for 0, 1 and N layers and it is the same. With the flag `False`, every FSDP module gets itself as its only backward-prefetch target. The list is then nonempty, so FSDP skips its implicit prefetch, and the self-target finds its own parameters already unsharded, so no extra all-gather happens.

**Example.**
```python
# EP=4, 3 layers, fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False
# main:  layers.2.pre_backward -> unshard(layers.2), prefetch unshard(layers.1)
#        => two layers' unsharded params live at once
# PR:    layers.2.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch([layers.2])
#        layers.2.pre_backward -> unshard(layers.2); self-target unshard() is a no-op
#        => one layer live; layers.1 is gathered only when its own pre_backward fires
# EP=1 with the same setting: early return at fsdp.py:517 -> implicit prefetch still runs, no error
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- there is no "Summary (human-written)" section from `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The author needs to write it. The description also says it "extends the existing wiring test", but `test_apply_fsdp_to_decoder_configures_backward_prefetch_policy` is a new test function.
2. No consumer and no value evidence. Nothing in this PR or later in the stack sets the flag to `False`: #5684 doesn't reference it, and #5676 only sets it in unit tests. The PR also gives no peak-memory number ("large-scale memory/performance ... not separately verified"). `rules/config.md` says to expose only options a verified recipe uses. Please name the recipe that will set it to `False` and give the measured peak-memory saving and throughput cost. Otherwise, hold the knob until that recipe lands.
3. `torchtitan/config/parallelism.py:69` -- the setting silently does nothing when EP=1. Apply it EP-independently or raise (inline).
4. `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:555` -- the self-target trick works around a missing FSDP2 API and depends on FSDP2 internals. Add a TODO with an upstream issue link (inline).

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/config/parallelism.py:64` -- new `enable_*` boolean; `fsdp_backward_prefetch` matches its siblings (inline).
- `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:287` -- the internal default duplicates the config default; make it a required keyword-only argument (inline).
- The numerics check compares against the earlier revision of this PR (`3449bed`), not `main`. The default-on path rewrites code that is on `main`, so the bitwise check should use `main` (`ff96670`) as its baseline. From reading the code I expect it to be identical.

### Questions
- Your motivation mentions memory-constrained PP/CUDA-graph recipes. Is dense (EP=1) PP also a target? If so, that supports applying the setting EP-independently.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Equivalence of the default path.** `main` sets: `lm_head -> [layers[-1]]` (only when norm and lm_head exist and there is at least one layer), each `layers[i] -> [layers[i-1]]`, and `layers[0] -> [tok_embeddings]` when tok_embeddings exists. The new order list, `[lm_head?] + reversed(layers) + [tok_embeddings?]`, built only when layers is nonempty, produces exactly these pairs. With weight tying, `lm_head`/`norm`/`tok_embeddings` share one FSDP state, as on `main`.
- **Disabled path.** `model.modules()` filtered on `FSDPModule` covers the root, the embedding/norm/head units, every layer (including MTP layers temporarily inserted by `apply_fsdp_to_mtp_decoder`), and nested units added later in the stack (#5676). Under tying, the three modules write the same shared state, which is fine. `tok_embeddings` with `unshard_in_backward=False` stays un-gathered, because `unshard()` returns early in PRE_BACKWARD.
- **Smaller alternative for the EP gap.** Move the `else` branch (self-pairs) above `if ep_degree == 1: return`, and keep the neighbor-pair branch where it is. About the same LoC, and the docstring caveats go away.
- **Test.** It is a cheap CPU mock test. It guards the self-target wiring, which would otherwise regress silently as higher memory. It doesn't check the actual claim (no implicit prefetch and no extra all-gather), because that is upstream behavior. That gap is one more reason for the upstream TODO.

</details>

Not verified: FSDP2 internals (`_pre_backward` default-prefetch condition, `unshard()` early return) were checked from my knowledge of upstream source, not against the installed torch version, because torch isn't installed in this runner. A maintainer still needs to review the core changes.

If you set `fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False` without EP, it silently does nothing: `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` returns at `if ep_degree == 1:` (fsdp.py:517) before the new branch runs. A dense or EP=1 run with this setting still gets FSDP's implicit backward prefetch and the memory it costs, and nothing tells the user. CLAUDE.md principle 8 says an unsupported combination should raise, not be ignored.

The self-target mechanism doesn't depend on EP, and the motivation you give (memory-constrained PP/CUDA-graph recipes) isn't EP-specific either. The smallest fix is to apply the `else` branch for every decoder by moving it above the `ep_degree == 1` return. That's about 5 moved lines, and the default path doesn't change. Then delete the "no effect without EP" sentence here and in the `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` docstring. If you really want it to stay EP-only, raise a `ValueError` in `ParallelismConfig.__post_init__` when it is `False` and `expert_parallel_degree == 1`.

     fsdp_defer_gradient_reduction: bool = False
     """Defer FSDP gradient reduction until the last accumulation step."""
 
+    fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch: bool = True
+    """Enable FSDP backward prefetching for expert-parallel models.
+

nodes.body:
The self-target trick is a workaround for something FSDP2 doesn't provide: there is no public way to turn off implicit backward prefetch. It also leans on two undocumented internals. First, `FSDPState._pre_backward` computes `default_prefetch = len(self._states_to_backward_prefetch) == 0`. Second, `FSDPParamGroup.unshard()` returns early when the group is already unsharded (or when `unshard_in_backward=False`, as on `tok_embeddings`). If either of these changes upstream, this path would silently start all-gathering again, or would gather a unit twice.

Per CLAUDE.md principle 3, please add a `TODO` here that links an upstream pytorch/pytorch issue asking for a public way to disable it, for example making an explicit empty list mean "no prefetch", or a `set_backward_prefetch(False)`. That way the trick can be deleted once upstream supports this.

                 [model.norm, model.lm_head]
             )
 
-    # set up explicit prefetching when EP is enabled for backward
-    # pyrefly: ignore [no-matching-overload]
-    reversed_transformer_blocks = list(reversed(model.layers.values()))
-    prev_transformer_blocks = reversed_transformer_blocks[1:] + [None]
-
-    if model.norm is not None and model.lm_head is not None and len(model.layers) > 0:
-        model.lm_head.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch([reversed_transformer_blocks[0]])
+    backward_prefetch_pairs: list[tuple[nn.Module, nn.Module]]
+    if enable_backward_prefetch:
+        # pyrefly: ignore [no-matching-overload]
+        backward_prefetch_order: list[nn.Module] = list(reversed(model.layers.values()))
+        if backward_prefetch_order:
+            if model.norm is not None and model.lm_head is not None:
+                backward_prefetch_order.insert(0, model.lm_head)
+            if model.tok_embeddings is not None:
+                backward_prefetch_order.append(model.tok_embeddings)
+        backward_prefetch_pairs = list(
+            zip(backward_prefetch_order, backward_prefetch_order[1:])
+        )
+    else:
+        # An empty explicit target list enables FSDP's implicit fallback
+        # prefetch. A self target keeps the list nonempty, but its own
+        # pre-backward hook has already prepared the parameters. This avoids
+        # an extra all-gather and live parameter unit.

This field is a policy toggle, not an optional component, so the closest sibling is `fsdp_defer_gradient_reduction: bool`. Consider renaming it `fsdp_backward_prefetch: bool = True`, and the parameter in `apply_fsdp_to_decoder`/`apply_fsdp_to_mtp_decoder` to `backward_prefetch`.

All three in-repo callers (`decoder.py`, `deepseek_v3/mtp.py`, `deepseek_v4/model.py`) already pass it explicitly. Consider making it a required keyword-only argument, here and in `apply_fsdp_to_mtp_decoder` (mtp.py:462). That way a new caller can't silently pick a value that differs from the config.

files.patch:
@@ -66,6 +66,76 @@ def param_dtype_override_fn(param: nn.Parameter) -> torch.dtype | None:
     assert mp_policy.param_dtype_override_fn is param_dtype_override_fn
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_backward_prefetch", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_layers", [0, 1, 3])
+def test_apply_fsdp_to_decoder_configures_backward_prefetch_policy(
+    enable_backward_prefetch: bool,
+    num_layers: int,
+) -> None:
+    """EP models may trade backward communication overlap for peak memory."""
+    model = _FSDPModule()
+    model.enable_weight_tying = False
+    model.tok_embeddings = _FSDPModule()
+    model.norm = _FSDPModule()
+    model.lm_head = _FSDPModule()
+    layers = [_FSDPModule() for _ in range(num_layers)]
+    for layer in layers:
+        layer.feed_forward = nn.Identity()
+        layer.feed_forward.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch = mock.Mock()
+    model.layers = nn.ModuleDict(
+        {str(index): layer for index, layer in enumerate(layers)}
+    )
+    fsdp_modules = (model, model.tok_embeddings, model.norm, model.lm_head, *layers)
+    for module in fsdp_modules:
+        module.set_gradient_divide_factor = mock.Mock()
+        module.set_modules_to_forward_prefetch = mock.Mock()
+        module.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch = mock.Mock()
+    dp_mesh = mock.Mock(mesh_dim_names=("dp_shard",))
+
+    with (
+        mock.patch("torchtitan.distributed.fsdp.fully_shard"),
+        mock.patch("torchtitan.distributed.fsdp.FSDPModule", _FSDPModule),
+        mock.patch(
+            "torchtitan.distributed.fsdp._fsdp_unit_holds_only_embedding_weights",
+            return_value=False,
+        ),
+    ):
+        apply_fsdp_to_decoder(
+            model,
+            dp_mesh,
+            param_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            reduce_dtype=torch.float32,
+            pp_enabled=True,
+            ep_degree=2,
+            enable_backward_prefetch=enable_backward_prefetch,
+        )

inline_comments.body:
If you set `fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False` without EP, it silently does nothing: `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` returns at `if ep_degree == 1:` (fsdp.py:517) before the new branch runs. A dense or EP=1 run with this setting still gets FSDP's implicit backward prefetch and the memory it costs, and nothing tells the user. CLAUDE.md principle 8 says an unsupported combination should raise, not be ignored.

The self-target mechanism doesn't depend on EP, and the motivation you give (memory-constrained PP/CUDA-graph recipes) isn't EP-specific either. The smallest fix is to apply the `else` branch for every decoder by moving it above the `ep_degree == 1` return. That's about 5 moved lines, and the default path doesn't change. Then delete the "no effect without EP" sentence here and in the `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` docstring. If you really want it to stay EP-only, raise a `ValueError` in `ParallelismConfig.__post_init__` when it is `False` and `expert_parallel_degree == 1`.

inline_comments.body:
The self-target trick is a workaround for something FSDP2 doesn't provide: there is no public way to turn off implicit backward prefetch. It also leans on two undocumented internals. First, `FSDPState._pre_backward` computes `default_prefetch = len(self._states_to_backward_prefetch) == 0`. Second, `FSDPParamGroup.unshard()` returns early when the group is already unsharded (or when `unshard_in_backward=False`, as on `tok_embeddings`). If either of these changes upstream, this path would silently start all-gathering again, or would gather a unit twice.

Per CLAUDE.md principle 3, please add a `TODO` here that links an upstream pytorch/pytorch issue asking for a public way to disable it, for example making an explicit empty list mean "no prefetch", or a `set_backward_prefetch(False)`. That way the trick can be deleted once upstream supports this.

**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 3m 9s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41135764218)

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Request changes** -- No recipe in the repo or the stack turns the new knob off, and it silently does nothing without EP. The mechanism works, but it relies on undocumented FSDP2 behavior and has no upstream TODO.

**What this PR does.** It adds `ParallelismConfig.fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch` (default `True`) and passes it to `apply_fsdp_to_decoder` and the MTP wrapper. With EP on and the flag `True`, the existing backward-prefetch chain (lm_head -> last layer -> ... -> first layer -> tok_embeddings) is rebuilt as a list of pairs. I checked the order against `main` for 0, 1 and N layers and it is the same. With the flag `False`, every FSDP module gets itself as its only backward-prefetch target. The list is then nonempty, so FSDP skips its implicit prefetch, and the self-target finds its own parameters already unsharded, so no extra all-gather happens.

**Example.**
```python
# EP=4, 3 layers, fsdp_enable_backward_prefetch=False
# main:  layers.2.pre_backward -> unshard(layers.2), prefetch unshard(layers.1)
#        => two layers' unsharded params live at once
# PR:    layers.2.set_modules_to_backward_prefetch([layers.2])
#        layers.2.pre_backward -> unshard(layers.2); self-target unshard() is a no-op
#        => one layer live; layers.1 is gathered only when its own pre_backward fires
# EP=1 with the same setting: early return at fsdp.py:517 -> implicit prefetch still runs, no error
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- there is no "Summary (human-written)" section from `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The author needs to write it. The description also says it "extends the existing wiring test", but `test_apply_fsdp_to_decoder_configures_backward_prefetch_policy` is a new test function.
2. No consumer and no value evidence. Nothing in this PR or later in the stack sets the flag to `False`: #5684 doesn't reference it, and #5676 only sets it in unit tests. The PR also gives no peak-memory number ("large-scale memory/performance ... not separately verified"). `rules/config.md` says to expose only options a verified recipe uses. Please name the recipe that will set it to `False` and give the measured peak-memory saving and throughput cost. Otherwise, hold the knob until that recipe lands.
3. `torchtitan/config/parallelism.py:69` -- the setting silently does nothing when EP=1. Apply it EP-independently or raise (inline).
4. `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:555` -- the self-target trick works around a missing FSDP2 API and depends on FSDP2 internals. Add a TODO with an upstream issue link (inline).

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/config/parallelism.py:64` -- new `enable_*` boolean; `fsdp_backward_prefetch` matches its siblings (inline).
- `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:287` -- the internal default duplicates the config default; make it a required keyword-only argument (inline).
- The numerics check compares against the earlier revision of this PR (`3449bed`), not `main`. The default-on path rewrites code that is on `main`, so the bitwise check should use `main` (`ff96670`) as its baseline. From reading the code I expect it to be identical.

### Questions
- Your motivation mentions memory-constrained PP/CUDA-graph recipes. Is dense (EP=1) PP also a target? If so, that supports applying the setting EP-independently.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Equivalence of the default path.** `main` sets: `lm_head -> [layers[-1]]` (only when norm and lm_head exist and there is at least one layer), each `layers[i] -> [layers[i-1]]`, and `layers[0] -> [tok_embeddings]` when tok_embeddings exists. The new order list, `[lm_head?] + reversed(layers) + [tok_embeddings?]`, built only when layers is nonempty, produces exactly these pairs. With weight tying, `lm_head`/`norm`/`tok_embeddings` share one FSDP state, as on `main`.
- **Disabled path.** `model.modules()` filtered on `FSDPModule` covers the root, the embedding/norm/head units, every layer (including MTP layers temporarily inserted by `apply_fsdp_to_mtp_decoder`), and nested units added later in the stack (#5676). Under tying, the three modules write the same shared state, which is fine. `tok_embeddings` with `unshard_in_backward=False` stays un-gathered, because `unshard()` returns early in PRE_BACKWARD.
- **Smaller alternative for the EP gap.** Move the `else` branch (self-pairs) above `if ep_degree == 1: return`, and keep the neighbor-pair branch where it is. About the same LoC, and the docstring caveats go away.
- **Test.** It is a cheap CPU mock test. It guards the self-target wiring, which would otherwise regress silently as higher memory. It doesn't check the actual claim (no implicit prefetch and no extra all-gather), because that is upstream behavior. That gap is one more reason for the upstream TODO.

</details>

Not verified: FSDP2 internals (`_pre_backward` default-prefetch condition, `unshard()` early return) were checked from my knowledge of upstream source, not against the installed torch version, because torch isn't installed in this runner. A maintainer still needs to review the core changes.
